bounded_statement: Each first-collection source unit r01–r08, which the task states is identified by k1 and measured by column a, appears on exactly three staged rows, and the workflow feeds all 24 resulting a-values into scipy's Mann-Whitney U test, a rank procedure that treats every entry as an independent observation; the same authorized units are therefore repeatedly entered into a row-independent procedure, with the reported U=288 arising from all 24 repeated entries per side.

counterevidence_considered.description: The task instructs applying the procedure to the complete staged row sequence, which could be read as authorizing every row's entry; however, this authorizes the rows as input, not treating three measurements of one declared unit as three independent observations.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: instruction to use complete row sequence

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

counterevidence_considered.description: The k2 codes (z01–z24) are all distinct, so the second collection's entries are not repeated; the issue is demonstrated only on the k1 side.

evidence.description: The task establishes that k1 identifies a first-collection source item measured by column a.
evidence.observed_value: k1 = source-unit identifier for column a

evidence.description: The same k1 unit appears on multiple rows: r01 occurs on three consecutive rows with three different a-values, and this three-rows-per-unit pattern runs through r08.
evidence.observed_value: 8 distinct r units across 24 rows, each contributing 3 a-values

evidence.description: All row-level a-values are fed unaggregated into a Mann-Whitney U test, which assumes each ranked entry is an independent observation.
evidence.observed_value: st.mannwhitneyu over 24 left entries from 8 units

source_refs.quoted_text:
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in staged]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in staged]
result = st.mannwhitneyu(left, right)

evidence.description: The selected report's U statistic of 288 is exactly half of 24×24=576, consistent with all 24 entries per side (including the repeated unit entries) being ranked in the produced result.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify by (1) checking whether equal r codes could denote distinct units — the task states k1 identifies a source item, giving no basis for that reading; (2) checking whether Mann-Whitney has any mechanism to handle clustered or repeated entries — it does not, and the U=288 value is consistent with 24 entries per side all being ranked; and (3) checking whether the storage-convention disclaimer covers within-column repetition — it only disclaims cross-column row pairing. The demonstrated verdict survived all three attempts.

root_cause: The workflow passes every row's a-value directly into st.mannwhitneyu without aggregating or deduplicating by the k1 unit identifier, so the three measurements per r-unit are ranked as three independent observations, inflating the effective first-collection sample from 8 units to 24 entries.
